summary: The main article describes the development of 'BecaP' as a phosphorus radical trap for deboronative and decarboxylative phosphonylation. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope tables for both methods, and schemes detailing the mechanism and synthetic applications like the synthesis of Phaclofen.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Biologically Relevant Phosphonates and Radical-Mediated Approaches to Aliphatic Phosphonates
items.description: Illustrates the biological significance of phosphonates and compares traditional radical approaches with the new BecaP-mediated strategy.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the Deboronative Phosphonylation
items.description: Lists reaction conditions, photocatalysts, and additives screened to optimize the yield of product 3a from trifluoroborate salt 1a.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate Scope for the Deboronative Phosphonylation with BecaP
items.description: Displays the variety of alkyl potassium trifluoroborate salts successfully converted to phosphonates, including drug derivatives.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Substrate Scope for the Decarboxylative Phosphonylation with BecaP
items.description: Shows the scope of N-hydroxyphthalimide esters derived from carboxylic acids that undergo phosphonylation using BecaP.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Comparative Substrate Scope for the Deboronative and Decarboxylative Phosphonylation with BecaP
items.description: Compares the yields of specific phosphonate products obtained via the deboronative (Method A) versus decarboxylative (Method B) pathways.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Mechanistic Studies and Proposed Mechanisms for the Deboronative and Decarboxylative Phosphonylations
items.description: Details radical clock experiments and the proposed catalytic cycles for both reductive and oxidative quenching pathways.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Gram-Scale Reactions, Product Diversification, and Application to the Synthesis of Phaclofen
items.description: Demonstrates the scalability of the reaction and the conversion of baclofen to phaclofen using the developed methodology.
